title: Introduction to the Sanctuary
description: Discover why the sanctuary message is central to understanding God's plan of salvation.

sections.title: Why Study the Sanctuary?
sections.content:
The sanctuary is not merely an ancient relic of Israel's history—it is a living revelation of God's plan to save humanity. When God instructed Moses to build the sanctuary, He said, "Let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them" (Exodus 25:8).

This was God's desire from the beginning: to dwell with His people. Sin had separated humanity from their Creator, but through the sanctuary service, God revealed how that separation would be healed.

The sanctuary message became especially significant after October 22, 1844. As early Adventist pioneers studied Scripture, they discovered that the sanctuary held the key to understanding Christ's ongoing ministry in heaven. Ellen G. White wrote that the subject of the sanctuary "was the key which unlocked the mystery of the disappointment of 1844. It opened to view a complete system of truth, connected and harmonious."
keyPoints: God's desire is to dwell among His people
The sanctuary reveals God's plan to heal the separation caused by sin
The sanctuary message explains the significance of 1844
It reveals Christ's ongoing heavenly ministry

cards.front: According to Exodus 25:8, why did God ask for a sanctuary to be built?
cards.back: That He may dwell among His people

cards.front: What event did the sanctuary message help explain?
What did Ellen G. White call the sanctuary subject?
cards.back: The key which unlocked the mystery of the disappointment of 1844

cards.front: Where is the true sanctuary that Christ ministers in?
cards.back: In heaven—the true tabernacle which the Lord pitched and not man

cards.front: What did the earthly sanctuary reveal?
cards.back: God's plan to save humanity and heal the separation caused by sin

questions.question: According to Exodus 25:8, what was God's purpose in having a sanctuary built?
options: To store the tablets of the law
To provide employment for the Levites
questions.explanation: God said, 'Let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them' (Exodus 25:8). God's primary purpose was relational—He wanted to be near His people.

questions.question: The earthly sanctuary was a copy of the heavenly sanctuary.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:5 tells us that the earthly priests served 'unto the example and shadow of heavenly things.' The earthly sanctuary was patterned after the true sanctuary in heaven.

questions.question: What historical event did the sanctuary message help early Adventists understand?
options: The fall of Jerusalem in 70 AD
questions.explanation: The sanctuary message was 'the key which unlocked the mystery of the disappointment of 1844,' helping Adventists understand what actually happened on that date.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 8:2, Christ is a minister of the sanctuary and of the true ___ which the Lord pitched.
questions.explanation: Hebrews 8:2 describes Christ as 'a minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.'

questions.question: The sanctuary message only relates to ancient Israel and has no relevance for Christians today.
questions.explanation: The sanctuary message reveals Christ's ongoing ministry in heaven and is central to understanding present truth. It shows us what Jesus is doing for us right now as our High Priest.
